result.rationale: The diff clearly shows a non-atomic read-then-write sequence in app-credential.ts: prisma.credential.findFirst is followed by either update or create in separate awaits, with the code even acknowledging it can't upsert. Two concurrent webhook requests could both pass the findFirst (no result) and both execute create, producing duplicate credentials for the same user/appId — a real race-condition correctness defect introduced by this new endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, the code checks for an existing credential via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` and then conditionally does `prisma.credential.create(...)` if none is found. This check-then-create pattern is not atomic and, under concurrent webhook requests for the same `userId`/`appSlug`, both requests can observe “no credential” and attempt `create`, potentially producing duplicates (if there is no DB uniqueness constraint) or causing a unique-constraint error (if there is one). The diff shows no transaction/upsert/locking to prevent this race.
